title: Dual base change
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with its finite-type $k$-scheme and coefficient conventions, and write $\mathcal C_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ for its supplied finite-Tor categories. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\
f'\downarrow && \downarrow f\\
Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y
\end{array}
$$
be a Cartesian square of separated finite-type $k$-schemes whose arrows are separated and of finite type. Use the canonical exchange and composition comparisons, with the identity, square-comparison and pasting normalizations of [fix-lem-exchanges], restricted to the domains supplied by the datum. There is a canonical natural isomorphism of functors $\mathcal C_{Y'}\to\mathcal C_X$,
$$
\beta_\square:Rf^!Rg_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg'_*Rf'^!,
$$
natural in the square through the adjoint comparison maps and compatible with horizontal and vertical pasting. More precisely, under the composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]
$$Lg^*Rf_!\dashv Rf^!Rg_*,\qquad Rf'_!Lg'^*\dashv Rg'_*Rf'^!,$$
$\beta_\square$ is the inverse of the conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of the canonical base-change isomorphism $\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*$; equivalently it is the conjugate of $\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$. If $g$ is proper, then $g'$ is proper, and under the proper-coincidence identifications $Ru_!\cong Ru_*$ of axiom (A4) of [def-sf-datum], the same isomorphism reads
$$Rf^!Rg_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg'_!Rf'^!.$$
All integral operations here are completed, and the rational and algebraically closed coefficient operations have the datum's scalar-localization and common-stage meanings; there is no assertion on unrestricted ambient categories.

proof.text: Put $A=Lg^*Rf_!$, $B=Rf'_!Lg'^*$, $R=Rf^!Rg_*$ and $T=Rg'_*Rf'^!$. The datum [def-sf-datum](A1) supplies the four individual adjunctions on $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y,\mathcal C_{X'},\mathcal C_{Y'}$. Applying the Hom-bijection construction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] twice gives $A\dashv R$ and $B\dashv T$. In particular $\operatorname{Hom}(AK,L)=\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!K,Rg_*L)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,RL)$, and the other chain is $\operatorname{Hom}(BK,L)=\operatorname{Hom}(Lg'^*K,Rf'^!L)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,TL)$. All objects in these chains lie in the categories stipulated by the datum, so no ambient exceptional adjoint is being used. Axiom (A2) supplies the specified natural isomorphism $\tau=\operatorname{Ex}_!:A\to B$.

source.place: Proof: A1, A2 and the two composite right adjoints

proof.text:
Let $\eta_A,\varepsilon_A$ and $\eta_B,\varepsilon_B$ be the units and counits just constructed. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to $\tau:A\to B$. Its conjugate is the natural transformation
$$\alpha:T\xrightarrow{\eta_A T}RAT\xrightarrow{R\tau T}RBT\xrightarrow{R\varepsilon_B}R.$$
Conjugate $\tau^{-1}$ in the other direction to obtain
$$\beta:R\xrightarrow{\eta_B R}TBR\xrightarrow{T\tau^{-1}R}TAR\xrightarrow{T\varepsilon_A}T.$$
That node's composition and identity clauses give $\alpha\circ\beta=(\tau^{-1}\circ\tau)^c=\mathrm{id}_R$ and $\beta\circ\alpha=(\tau\circ\tau^{-1})^c=\mathrm{id}_T$. Thus $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ is the claimed isomorphism. Its component at any $L\in\mathcal C_{Y'}$ is exactly this unit--inverse-exchange--counit composite; in particular it is a natural transformation in $L$, rather than just an objectwise choice of isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof: uniqueness of right adjoints and the mate of Ex_!; direction made explicit

proof.text:
For naturality in the square, [fix-lem-exchanges](1) gives commutative exchange diagrams through the canonical square comparisons. Write the left and right exchange functors for two squares as $A_i\dashv R_i$, $B_i\dashv T_i$, $\tau_i:A_i\to B_i$, with $A_i,B_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$. A square comparison with endpoint functors $G:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$, $H:\mathcal D_1\to\mathcal D_2$ has comparison transformations $a:A_2G\to HA_1$, $b:B_2G\to HB_1$, and the exchange diagram is
$$b\circ(\tau_2G)=(H\tau_1)\circ a.$$
Their mates have types $a^\flat:GR_1\to R_2H$ and $b^\flat:GT_1\to T_2H$. Put $\alpha_i=\tau_i^c$, $\beta_i=\alpha_i^{-1}$ as in Step 2. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](3a) to the left side and (3b) to the right side gives
$$(\alpha_2H)\circ b^\flat=a^\flat\circ(G\alpha_1).$$
Postcompose with $\beta_2H$ and precompose with $G\beta_1$; the inverse equations of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] cancel $\alpha_i\beta_i$ and yield
$$b^\flat\circ(G\beta_1)=(\beta_2H)\circ a^\flat:GR_1\longrightarrow T_2H.$$
This is exactly the required naturality diagram through the adjoint comparison maps, including endpoint functors. For fixed endpoints take $G,H$ to be identities. Comparisons formed by composing or whiskering square data have these same mates by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1)--(2), so the displayed equation applies to them as well.

source.place: Proof: naturality of the mate; square-comparison compatibility

proof.text:
For pasting, use the two explicit exchange equations of [fix-lem-exchanges](2). Conjugation reverses composition by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], and the whiskered conjugates are identified by the two pasting clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with the pasted units and counits of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Taking inverses gives the following formulas, which also specify the claimed compatibility. For horizontal pasting with $h:Y''\to Y'$ and $h':X''\to X'$, write $f'':X''\to Y''$ for the further base change and $\beta_g,\beta_h$ for the two dual exchanges. Then
$$\beta_{gh}=(Rg'_*\beta_h)\circ(\beta_g Rh_*):Rf^!Rg_*Rh_*\longrightarrow Rg'_*Rh'_*Rf''^!.$$
For vertical pasting with $e:W\to X$, its base change $e':W'\to X'$, and $g'':W'\to W$, write $\beta_e:Re^!Rg'_*\to Rg''_*Re'^!$. Then
$$\beta_{fe}=(\beta_e Rf'^!)\circ(Re^!\beta_f):Re^!Rf^!Rg_*\longrightarrow Rg''_*Re'^!Rf'^!.$$
Insert the ordinary direct-image composition comparisons and their adjoint pullback comparisons from the pasted (A1) datum; for the exceptional comparisons insert $R(fe)^!\cong Re^!Rf^!$ and $R(f'e')^!\cong Re'^!Rf'^!$, which [lem-sf-mate] identifies as the conjugates of compact-support composition. The formulas have the stated domains and codomains. Since identity exchange is the identity by [fix-lem-exchanges](2), conjugation and inversion also give identity dual exchange. These computations prove both kinds of pasting, rather than asserting an unspecified coherence of right-adjoint choices.

source.place: Proof: compatibility with pasting by mate calculus

proof.text:
Suppose $g$ is proper. In the square rotated so that $g$ is the morphism being pulled back, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] says that its base change $g'$ is proper. Let $c_g:Rg_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*$ and $c_{g'}:Rg'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg'_*$ be the identifications supplied by [def-sf-datum](A4). The required proper-case arrow is the explicit composite
$$Rf^!Rg_!\xrightarrow{Rf^!c_g}Rf^!Rg_*\xrightarrow{\beta_\square}Rg'_*Rf'^!\xrightarrow{c_{g'}^{-1}Rf'^!}Rg'_!Rf'^!.$$
Each factor is an isomorphism, so this is an isomorphism. It is exactly the previously constructed arrow expressed through $c_g,c_{g'}$, and hence retains its naturality and pasting compatibilities when the same canonical identifications are inserted.
